It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} of {{ill|Shimashimo district|ja|島下郡|zh|岛下郡|qid=Q10976940}}, {{ill|Settsu Province|ca|Província de Settsu|cs|Provincie Seccu|de|Provinz Settsu|eo|Provinco Seccu|es|Provincia de Settsu|fa|ولایت ستسو|fr|Province de Settsu|gl|Provincia de Settsu|hak|Settsu-koet|id|Provinsi Settsu|it|Settsu (provincia)|ja|摂津国|ko|셋쓰국|lt|Seccu žemė|nl|Settsu (provincie)|pt|Província de Settsu|ru|Сэтцу (провинция)|simple|Settsu Province|sk|Seccu (provincia)|sr|Провинција Сецу|tr|Settsu (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Сеццу|zh|攝津國|zh_min_nan|Settu-kok|zh_yue|攝津國|qid=Q864163}}, listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}. {{nihongo|'''Sukuku Shrine'''|須久久神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}. It is located in {{ill|Settsu Province|ca|Província de Settsu|cs|Provincie Seccu|de|Provinz Settsu|eo|Provinco Seccu|es|Provincia de Settsu|fa|ولایت ستسو|fr|Province de Settsu|gl|Provincia de Settsu|hak|Settsu-koet|id|Provinsi Settsu|it|Settsu (provincia)|ja|摂津国|ko|셋쓰국|lt|Seccu žemė|nl|Settsu (provincie)|pt|Província de Settsu|ru|Сэтцу (провинция)|simple|Settsu Province|sk|Seccu (provincia)|sr|Провинција Сецу|tr|Settsu (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Сеццу|zh|攝津國|zh_min_nan|Settu-kok|zh_yue|攝津國|qid=Q864163|lt=Settsu Province}}.

== Enshrined deities ==
Currently, the shrine enshrines two deities:
* {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|abstract|Q272993|ar|سوسانو|azb|سوسانو|bcl|Susanoo|be|Сусанаа|bg|Сусаноо|ca|Susanoo|cs|Susanoo|da|Susa-no-o|de|Susanoo|el|Σουσάνoο|eo|Susanoo|es|Susanoo|eu|Susanoo|fa|سوسانو (خدا)|fi|Susanoo|fr|Susanoo|hr|Susano|hu|Szuszanoo|hy|Սուսանո|id|Susanoo|it|Susanoo|ja|スサノオ|ka|სუსანოო-ნო-მიკოტო|ko|스사노오|la|Susano'o|lb|Susanoo|mni|ꯁꯨꯁꯅꯨ-ꯅꯣ-ꯃꯤꯀꯣꯇꯣ|nl|Susanoo|pl|Susanoo|pt|Susanoo|ro|Susanoo|rsk|Сусано|ru|Сусаноо|simple|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|sl|Susanovo|sr|Сусаноо|su|Susanoo|sv|Susanoo|ta|சுசானவோ|th|ซูซาโนโอะ|tok|jan sewi Susano|tr|Susanoo|uk|Сусаноо|vi|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|zh|素戔嗚尊|zh_min_nan|Susanoo|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}
* {{ill|Kushinadahime|de|Kushinadahime|es|Kushinadahime|fr|Kushinada-hime|it|Kushinadahime|ja|クシナダヒメ|mni|ꯀꯨꯁꯤꯅꯗꯍꯤꯃꯦ|ru|Кусинада-химэ|simple|Kushinadahime|sr|Кушинадахиме|zh|櫛名田比賣|qid=Q505469|lt=Inadahime-no-Mikoto}}

== History ==
According to the “Jingū Zōreishū,” on April 5 of {{ill|Tenpyō|br|Tenpyō|ca|Era Tenpyō|de|Tempyō|es|Tenpyō|fa|تنپیو|fr|Ère Tenpyō|ia|Tenpyo|id|Tempyō|it|Tenpyō|ja|天平|ko|덴표|no|Tenpyō|pt|Tenpyō|ru|Тэмпё|simple|Tenpyō|sr|Тенпјо|tr|Tenpyō|uk|Темпьо (ненґо)|zh|天平 (日本)|zh_yue|天平 (日本)|qid=Q1199879}} 12 (740), the Right Minister {{ill|Ōnakatomi no Kiyomaro|fr|Ōnakatomi no Kiyomaro|ja|大中臣清麻呂|pt|Ōnakatomi no Kiyomaro|qid=Q11431854|lt=Nakatomi Kiyomaro}} secluded himself at this site and enshrined his ancestral deity near his residence. Yukihiko Tembō states that the shrine originally enshrined {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|fr|Ama-no-Koyane-no-mikoto|it|Ame-no-Koyane|ja|天児屋命|ko|아메노코야네|mni|ꯑꯃꯦ-ꯅꯣ-ꯀꯣꯌꯅꯦ|pt|Ame-no-Koyane|ru|Амэ-но коянэ-но микото|simple|Ame-no-Koyane|zh|天兒屋命|qid=Q2564508|lt=Amenokoyane-no-Mikoto}}. In the {{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448}} Jinmyōchō, it is recorded as “Sukuku Shrine, two seats, Kuwahazama,” with the other seat being {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Shimizu, Ibaraki, Osaka)|ja|春日神社 (茨木市清水)|zh|春日神社 (茨木市清水)|qid=Q11513674|lt=Kasuga Shrine}}. In ancient times, both sites were part of Shukushō, but in March of {{ill|Meireki|eo|Meireki|fa|می‌رکی|fr|Ère Meireki|ja|明暦|ko|메이레키|ru|Мэйрэки|simple|Meireki|sr|Меиреки|sv|Meireki|th|เมเรกิ|tr|Meireki|zh|明曆|qid=Q1192766}} 1 (1655) they were divided into two villages, and today the name refers only to this shrine.
In Meiji 5 (1872), it was ranked as a village shrine.
